facts.fact: As of 2026-10-16, FRED ICSA has no observation for the week ending 2026-10-17; the latest observation is the week ending 2026-10-10, and the next release date shown is 2026-10-22.
On 2026-10-15, the Department of Labor's first published seasonally adjusted initial claims for the week ending 2026-10-10 were 199,000.

That 199,000 figure is not above 199,000; the four prior revised weekly levels on the 2026-10-15 FRED vintage were 198,000 (2026-09-12), 198,000 (2026-09-19), 199,000 (2026-09-26), and 198,000 (2026-10-03).

The first published level for the week ending 2026-10-03 was 197,000; the 2026-10-15 release revised it to 198,000.
Resolution of the 2026-10-17 week uses only the first published ICSA value.

The FRED release calendar lists the Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims Report for Thursday, 2026-10-22, at 7:30 a.m., and that Thursday is not among ETA's listed holiday exceptions (which move the release off Thursday).

ETA states the weekly claims news release is published each Thursday at 8:30 a.m.
EST except when Thursday is a federal holiday.

uncertainties: The first published ICSA value for the week ending 2026-10-17 does not exist yet and is scheduled for release on 2026-10-22.
A print of exactly 199,000 would not be above 199,000; recent revised weeks have sat at 198,000 or 199,000.
Seasonal factors for the week ending 2026-10-17 are not in the 2026-10-15 release, and the prior week's unadjusted change already differed from the factor the Department had expected.
The prior week's first print was revised by 1,000 claims, so the level that will be revised later can differ from the first print that decides this question.
No advance state-by-state initial-claims changes for the week ending 2026-10-17 were in the 2026-10-15 release.

UNEMPLOYMENT INSURANCE WEEKLY CLAIMS
SEASONALLY ADJUSTED DATA
In the week ending October 10, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial claims was 199,000, an increase of
1,000 from the previous week's revised level.
The previous week's level was revised up by 1,000 from 197,000 to
198,000.
The 4-week moving average was 198,500, an increase of 250 from the previous week's revised average.
The
previous week's average was revised up by 250 from 198,000 to 198,250.
The advance seasonally adjusted insured unemployment rate was 1.1 percent for the week ending October 3,
unchanged from the previous week's unrevised rate.
The advance number for seasonally adjusted insured
unemployment during the week ending October 3 was 1,710,000, a decrease of 4,000 from the previous week's revised
level.
The previous week's level was revised down by 2,000 from 1,716,000 to 1,714,000.
The 4-week moving average
was 1,708,750, a decrease of 1,750 from the previous week's revised average.
The previous week's average was revised
down by 500 from 1,711,000 to 1,710,500.
2
UNADJUSTED DATA
The advance number of actual initial claims under state programs, unadjusted, totaled 190,626 in the week ending
October 10, an increase of 19,456 (or 11.4 percent) from the previous week.
The seasonal factors had expected an
increase of 18,799 (or 11.0 percent) from the previous week.
There were 210,777 initial claims in the comparable week
in 2025.
The advance unadjusted insured unemployment rate was 1.0 percent during the week ending October 3, unchanged from
the prior week.
The advance unadjusted level of insured unemployment in state programs totaled 1,469,083, a decrease
of 33,813 (or -2.2 percent) from the preceding week.
The seasonal factors had expected a decrease of 30,846 (or -2.1
percent) from the previous week.
A year earlier the rate was 1.1 percent and the volume was 1,651,988.
The total number of continued weeks claimed for benefits in all programs for the week ending September 26 was
1,525,589, an increase of 5,512 from the previous week.
There were 1,716,298 weekly claims filed for benefits in all
programs in the comparable week in 2025.
No state was triggered "on" the Extended Benefits program during the week ending September 26.
